newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Senate starts probe of lottery - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Senate starts probe of lottery - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Senate Committee on Post Audit and Oversight started a probe of the state Lottery's use of coupons, advertising and other potential problems, Boston Globe reported Friday.

At the same time, Auditor Joseph DeNucci's office is finishing its own investigation of the $3 billion a year agency, and has found a number of irregularities in its financial practices, the Globe quoted unidentified sources as saying. The final report is due out in six to eight weeks.
The Senate probe will focus on several areas, according to Sen. Cheryl Jacques, D-Needham, who chairs the committee.

The questions include whether the lottery dodged the $400,000 cap on advertising by paying for ads with its own coupons, potential losses of state revenue associated with coupons, and whether the agency targets low-income neighborhoods in its marketing, the paper said.
Another issue that will be examined is whether lottery sales agents play the games themselves, a practice that might give them an insiders' edge.
A spokeswoman for the lottery dismissed the legislative probe, telling the Globe "This is Beacon Hill, and this is nothing more than partisan politics."
